source_text: CAPUT VIGESIMUM SECUNDUM, De pace conscientiae. PAX CONSCIENTIAE est tranquillitas animi in homine credente in Christum, qua fit ut neque perturbetur comminationibus legis, neque frangatur adversis, sed iuxta promissionem divinam liberationem gloriosam ab omnibus quae in hac vita molesta sunt certo expectet tandemque adipiscatur. Oritur a fide reconciliationis cum Deo per D.N.I.C. (Rom. 5:1); fovetur spe quae non confundit; conservatur studio bonae conscientiae.
english: CHAPTER TWENTY-TWO. On peace of conscience.

PEACE OF CONSCIENCE is tranquillity of soul in one who believes in Christ, such that he is neither disturbed by the law's threatenings nor broken by adversities, but according to the divine promise surely expects and at last obtains glorious liberation from all that troubles this life.
It arises from faith in reconciliation with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Rom. 5:1); it is fostered by hope that does not put to shame; it is kept by zeal for a good conscience.

source_text: Haec est pax quam Angeli Christo nato pastoribus optarunt. Qui vere illuminatus verbo et Spiritu credit Christum passione et morte salutem acquisivisse et per baptismum applicuisse, tranquilla conscientia esse potest. Totum cor dulcedine caelestis pacis conditum est; etiamsi reliquum peccatum in carne sentiat, in Domino laetatur, novit Servatorem peccata in se recepisse et satisfecisse.
english: This is the peace the angels wished the shepherds at Christ's birth. Whoever is truly illumined by word and Spirit and believes Christ acquired salvation by passion and death and applied it in baptism can have a tranquil conscience.
The whole heart is seasoned with heavenly peace's sweetness; even sensing remaining sin in the flesh, he rejoices in the Lord, knowing the Savior took his sins and made satisfaction.

source_text: Fumus irae Dei a lege obiectus non reformidatur a pacifico: ubi non est peccatum, non est ira ut merces; castigatio filiorum pacem scientiae non tollit. Chrysostomus monet quotidianum iudicium conscientiae: sedeat mens iudex in animam; scrutare delicta; accusata tua vitia non aliena; ante forum vocata conscientia rationem expetat verborum, operum, cogitationum.
english: The smoke of God's wrath held forth by the law does not terrify the one at peace: where there is no sin, there is no wrath as wages; a father's chastening does not remove the peace of knowledge.

Chrysostom urges a daily tribunal of conscience: let the mind sit as judge over the soul; search out faults; accuse your own vices not others'; before the day, call conscience to account for words, works, and thoughts.

source_text: Absolvendus omni studio caveat ne dubitet sibi remissa esse apud Deum peccata. Stare tenetur alterius iudicio non propter praelatum sed propter verbum Christi: Quodcunque solveris super terram. Fides huius verbi faciet pacem conscientiae. Qui pacem alia via quaerit, puta experientia intus, Deum tentare videtur. Tantum habebis pacis quantum credideris verbo. Lutherus resol. de virt. indulg.: etiamsi millies a papa absolvatur, qui verbo non credit nunquam erit quietus.
english: Let the one being absolved take every care not to doubt that his sins are remitted before God. He is bound to stand by another's judgment not because of the prelate but because of Christ's word: Whatever you loose on earth. Faith in that word will make peace of conscience.

Whoever seeks peace another way—say by inward experience—seems to tempt God. You will have as much peace as you believe the word. Luther: even if absolved a thousand times by the pope himself, one who does not believe the word will never be at rest.

source_text: X. Consummatio pacis conscientiae et portus verae tranquillitatis, in quem Theologia nostra penetrare cupimus, est VITA AETERNA—finis hominis absolute summus (lib. II cap.14). Proinde nos quoque, cum tanta nos circumdet nubes testium, abiecto omni pondere et peccato, per tolerantiam stadium decurramus, intuentes in fidei ducem et consummatorem IESUM (Heb. 12:1-4; 1 Pet. 1:3-9). FINIS.
english: X. The consummation of peace of conscience and the harbor of true tranquillity, into which our Theology desires to penetrate, is ETERNAL LIFE—the absolutely highest end of man.
Therefore we too, surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, casting aside every weight and sin, must run the race with endurance, looking to Jesus the pioneer and perfecter of faith.
THE END. Liber IV Cap. 22 and the Syntagma densify close at PHYS 1363 FINIS. Index Authorum (PHYS ~1370–1372) is index matter, not densified as treatise body.
